speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for stating you have episodic cough and shortness of breath. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have any known history of asthma or allergies?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned symptoms starting 8 weeks ago, including fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion; have you been evaluated or treated for an infection at that time? Given the chronic cough and shortness of breath, I am also considering environmental triggers or cardiac issues; do you have any known heart conditions or do you smoke?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious reactive airway disease (post-viral cough).

The history of an upper respiratory infection followed by a one-month history of nocturnal and exertional dyspnea and cough is highly suggestive of airway hyperresponsiveness or early asthma triggered by the infection. No further testing is required at this time.
